newsitem.title: USA: Tambrands posts higher profit despite sales slip.
newsitem.headline: Tambrands posts higher profit despite sales slip.

text.p: Tambrands Inc., the world's leading manufacturer of tampons, said Friday that it managed to boost its first-quarter profits by 3 percent despite a slight decline in sales.

Tambrands, which has agreed to be acquired by Procter & Gamble Co. after six decades as an independent company, said its net income for the three months ended March 31 grew to $24.3 million, or 66 cents a share, from $23.6 million, or 64 cents a share, in the year-ago period.
Tambrands, which is based in White Plains, N.Y., said its net sales slipped to $168.2 million from $169.0 million in 1996, which was an especially goood quarter for the company.
The company markets its products in 150 countries.

"Tambrands is off to a good start in 1997, with volume comparable to a particularly strong first quarter last year and solid market shares on our new product entries in several countries," Chairman Edward Fogarty said in a statement.
The company said its increased its profit despite an increase in the cost of products sold, which was primarily due to transitional costs associated with the previously announced restructuring.

It added that marketing, selling and distribution costs fell in the quarter due to the timing of the a new advertising campaign, which began in March. Administrative costs were also favourable due to continuing efforts to lower expenses.
Tambrands' stock was unchanged at $47.375 in early afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
